reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a holiday beauty haul featuring ordinary cosmetic items and a random Ulta gift-card giveaway with no purchase necessary. The giveaway requires Ebates membership and a Google form, while the separate welcome bonus and affiliate links disclose sign-up, purchase, and possible creator commission conditions. These described activities are framed as sponsored promotion, with no established false claims, hidden destination behavior, credential theft, victim loss, or failed reward delivery.

citations.quote: I partnered with Ebates and they are giving my subscribers money, honey. 10 winners are going. To win $200 gift cards from Ulta.
Must be an Ebates member, If you don't have one already, sign up for an Ebates account using the link below: No purchase necessary.
Fill out this Google form and submit!
Hey guys, welcome back to my channel. It's been a hot minute since I've done a haul. So today I'm. Going to be doing a holiday haul for you guys.
Get $10 Welcome Bonus when you sign up and make a $25+ purchase with Ebates

opening.argument: The video links a substantial reward to a concrete participation path. It advertises ten $200 Ulta gift cards, then directs viewers to become Ebates members and submit a Google form. That is not merely discussion of cosmetics: the promised gift-card benefit is presented alongside account registration and form submission, making the reward conditional on viewer action. The separate Ebates offer also ties a $10 bonus to signing up and making a $25+ purchase. Taken together, the presentation solicits registration, submission, and potentially spending in exchange for rewards, which fits a low-barrier reward acquisition pattern even though the speaker calls it a giveaway.

citations.quote: 10 winners are going. To win $200 gift cards from Ulta.

Fill out this Google form and submit!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats “no purchase necessary” as resolving the concern, but the described entry still requires Ebates membership and a Google-form submission. The same material prominently promotes a separate bonus requiring a $25+ purchase, so viewers are being steered toward multiple reward-linked actions. Calling the process a partnership or giveaway does not establish that the advertised reward is independently verifiable or that the linked registration and form are risk-free.

citations.quote: No purchase necessary.
Must be an Ebates member
Get $10 Welcome Bonus when you sign up and make a $25+ purchase with Ebates

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited instructions show an entry mechanism, but they do not show that viewers must pay to enter: the terms expressly say “No purchase necessary.” The $25+ purchase condition belongs to a separately described welcome bonus, not the ten gift-card giveaway. Nothing in the quoted material establishes that the gift cards were unavailable, that the form harvested credentials, or that anyone suffered a loss.

citations.quote: No purchase necessary.
Get $10 Welcome Bonus when you sign up and make a $25+ purchase with Ebates
10 Winners will be emailed directly by 11/30.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an unusually attractive $200 gift-card reward, external destinations, a Google form, and a limited entry window. The description gives a short run from November 21 through November 27 and tells viewers to sign up through an Ebates link before submitting the form. The speaker also emphasizes that the giveaway is “100% random,” while offering no cited mechanism for independently checking selection or delivery. Those features create urgency and move viewers away from the video into an account-and-form flow, making the promotion resemble a reward solicitation rather than a harmless haul.

citations.quote: 10 winners are going. To win $200 gift cards from Ulta.
Giveaway is live from 11/21/16 - 11/27/16.
Fill out this Google form and submit!
GOOD LUCK as this will be 100% random.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense lists the cosmetics and calls the promotion ordinary, but that does not answer the combination of a high-value reward, a deadline, an external account link, and a separate form. “Random” describes selection, not proof that the process is genuine or that winners will receive anything. The presence of affiliate disclosure also confirms that the description is directing viewers toward commercial links, rather than merely sharing neutral information.

citations.quote: Giveaway closes 11/27/16 11:59PM PST.
http://www.ebates.com/desiperkins
This video and description may contain affiliate links

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are visible promotional conditions, not evidence of concealment: the dates, random-selection statement, Ebates requirement, and Google-form step are disclosed in the supplied material. A deadline does not prove deceptive urgency, and the quoted sources do not establish that the links were malicious, that the form requested sensitive information, or that the $200 cards were not awarded.

citations.quote: Giveaway closes 11/27/16 11:59PM PST.
GOOD LUCK as this will be 100% random.
No purchase necessary.

opening.argument: Although the video is framed as a holiday beauty haul, its own closing directs viewers to participate in the linked promotion. The speaker introduces the giveaway before the products, says the details will be in the description, and ends by telling viewers to enter and check the description. The product discussion therefore supplies an attention-grabbing consumer frame around a call to register and submit a form. The disclosure that affiliate links may generate a commission further shows that the surrounding haul is functioning as commercial steering, not just an independent review.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the main subject a haul does not change how the video directs viewers to act. The speaker explicitly places the giveaway instructions in the description and invites entry at the end, while the description contains links and a commission disclosure. The cosmetic framing can make the solicitation feel familiar and trustworthy, but it does not remove the reward-for-action pathway.
